theme: Accessibility and JS-interop correctness of a small Blazor Web App + Razor Pages room-booking portal

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The selected room photo is an bound to the photo URL with no alt, aria-label or aria-labelledby. The photo is the main content of the room page (it shows the layout and furniture the visitor is booking); a screen reader announces nothing useful.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The narrated room walk-through plays in a <video controls> with no captions <track>: the narration (capacity, accessible entrance, what equipment is in the room) is lost to deaf and hard-of-hearing visitors (WCAG 1.2.2).

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The 'next week' calendar button contains only an inline arrow <svg aria-hidden="true"> and has no text, aria-label, aria-labelledby or title: it has no accessible name, so assistive technology announces just 'button' (WCAG 4.1.2).

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The bookings filter <input> is named only by its placeholder: no <label>, no aria-label/aria-labelledby. A placeholder is not a label (it disappears on input and is not reliably announced) (WCAG 1.3.1, 4.1.2).

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The staff area's layout (every Razor Pages admin page renders inside it) opens <html> with no lang attribute, so assistive technology cannot choose pronunciation rules for any admin page (WCAG 3.1.1). The public Blazor host page declares lang; this one was written separately and omits it.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The settings page goes from its <h1> straight to <h3> section headings in one render: the h2 level is skipped, so heading navigation presents a broken outline (WCAG 1.3.1).

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: Each booked calendar slot is a <div> with an @onclick that opens the booking's detail panel (reference, times, attendees, organiser), but it has no role, no tabindex and no key handler, and nothing else in the page opens that panel: keyboard users cannot reach a booking's details at all (WCAG 2.1.1).

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The organiser-name field carries tabindex="1": a positive tabindex pulls it ahead of the skip link and the site navigation and fights the DOM order (WCAG 2.4.3).

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: 'Cancel booking' is an <a href="#"> whose @onclick performs an action: a button dressed as a link — announced as a link, not activated by Space, and a no-op jump without the circuit.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: A hand-rolled modal: a <div role="dialog"> over a backdrop with no aria-modal, no initial focus move into the dialog, no focus containment, no Escape handling and no focus return to the control that opened it. Keyboard focus stays on the page behind the overlay (WCAG 2.4.3).

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The 'E-mail reminders' toggle is a focusable role="switch" with click and key handlers but no aria-checked: the switch role requires aria-checked, so its on/off state is never exposed (only a CSS class changes) (WCAG 4.1.2).

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: Free-slot labels are normal-size text in #a3a3a3 on #ffffff — a contrast ratio of about 2.5:1, below the 4.5:1 AA minimum for normal text (WCAG 1.4.3).

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The home-page hero <video> starts on load (autoplay), loops forever and has no controls and no pause mechanism. It is muted, so WCAG 1.4.2 does not apply, but it is moving content that starts automatically and lasts more than five seconds with no way to pause, stop or hide it (WCAG 2.2.2).

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The loading skeleton's <style> block runs an infinite shimmer @keyframes animation with no prefers-reduced-motion guard anywhere, so motion-sensitive users cannot turn it off (WCAG 2.3.3).

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: Toasts slide in with an animation declared unconditionally in the component stylesheet, with no prefers-reduced-motion query, so the motion cannot be turned off (WCAG 2.3.3).

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The admin layout's <style> block sets outline: none on the toolbar buttons and declares no :focus or :focus-visible style anywhere: keyboard users cannot see which toolbar action has focus (WCAG 2.4.7).

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The navigation links' :focus rule removes the outline (outline: none) and the stylesheet gives no other focus style for them: the focused link is invisible to a keyboard user (WCAG 2.4.7).

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The attendees field's error message is rendered as a paragraph after the input but is tied to nothing: the input has no aria-describedby/aria-errormessage and no aria-invalid, and the message is not in a live region, so a screen-reader user is not told the field is wrong or why (WCAG 3.3.1, 1.3.1).

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The room description is cast to MarkupString and rendered as raw HTML. It is free HTML typed by staff in the admin area and stored verbatim (no sanitisation on save or render), so a script or event-handler attribute in a description runs in every visitor's browser: stored XSS (CWE-79). The notice banner sanitises; this path does not.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The component invokes a function by string name on the room-map script object that the script no longer defines (it was renamed in the script and the C# call was not updated): the interop call fails at run time, and the room is never highlighted on the map.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The calendar-file download invokes a string-named function on the export script object that no script defines under that name (the script exports it under another name): clicking 'Add to calendar' throws a JSException at run time.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: Nothing enforces accessibility: no automated accessibility assertion runs over the rendered markup in the component tests, no browser-based accessibility check exists, and CI runs neither. Every markup plant in this repository would be caught by such a check.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The foyer illustration's alt text is its file name: a file name is not a text equivalent of the image (WCAG 1.1.1).

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The link to the hire terms reads 'click here': out of context (a links list, a screen reader's link navigation) it says nothing about its destination (WCAG 2.4.4).

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The hourly-rate field's label reads 'Value': it does not say what the field is (the label of a generic key/value row copied into the form), so a user navigating by form fields hears 'Value, edit text' (WCAG 2.4.6).

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: The wave divider in the footer is purely decorative and is marked so with alt="": the correct text alternative for decoration is the empty one (WCAG 1.1.1, technique H67).

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: The hero video is muted footage with no audio track content to caption: captions (WCAG 1.2.2) are owed for audio, and there is none. (Its autoplay is a different defect, BA-013.)

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: The 'previous week' button is icon-only but carries aria-label="Previous week": it has an accessible name.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: The room search input's <label for> is visually hidden with a clip-based class, which keeps it in the accessibility tree: the input is programmatically labelled.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: Each amenity chip is a <span> with @onclick, but also role="checkbox", aria-checked, tabindex="0" and an @onkeydown handler for Space and Enter: a keyboard-operable custom checkbox.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: The skip link's href="#main-content" is a real fragment target (the <main id="main-content">), not a placeholder href.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: 'Show more rooms' is a native <button type="button"> styled to look like a link: fully keyboard-operable with the correct role.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: The booking summary is a native <dialog> opened with showModal() through a JS module: the browser moves focus into it, makes the page behind inert, closes it on Escape and returns focus to the previously focused control. No hand-written focus code is needed.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: The hero title is #ffffff on #2f8f9d at 2.25rem / 700 (36px bold): about 3.8:1 — below 4.5:1 but above the 3:1 AA minimum for large text, and the same rule sets the large size (WCAG 1.4.3).

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: Disabled buttons use a low-contrast pair on purpose: text of inactive user-interface components is exempt from the contrast minimum (WCAG 1.4.3).

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: The 'saved' tick animation is declared only inside @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference): users who ask for reduced motion get no animation.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: h1:focus { outline: none } removes the ring only from the page heading that the router focuses programmatically after navigation (tabindex -1, not in the tab order) — no keyboard-operable control loses its focus indicator.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: The chips drop the outline only for :focus:not(:focus-visible) (mouse focus) and draw a high-contrast :focus-visible ring for keyboard focus: the focus indicator is replaced, not removed.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: The card's <h3> is rendered inside the rooms list under the page's <h2> 'Available rooms': in the composed page there is no skipped level, although the component file on its own starts at h3.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: A Razor Page with a route template (@page "{id:guid}") is not a Blazor routed component: its document title is the admin layout's <title>, filled from ViewData["Title"], which this page sets, and its outline is one <h1>. The page as a whole is correct for page structure (whole-file trap since v1.0.0 iteration 1: the claim is about the page, not one line).

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: The notice HTML is passed through an allow-list HTML sanitiser (no script, no event-handler attributes, no javascript: URLs) before it is cast to MarkupString.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: aria-hidden="true" sits on the decorative <svg> icon inside a button that is named by aria-label; the svg itself is not focusable, so nothing focusable is hidden.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: role="checkbox" carries its required aria-checked state (bound to the chip's selection as the strings 'true'/'false').

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: The e-mail field's error is associated: the input sets aria-invalid and aria-describedby naming the error element's id, so the error is announced with the field.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: navigator.clipboard.writeText is a browser API: it is defined by the platform, not by any first-party script, and resolves at run time.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: The function is invoked on the JS module imported from the dialog script, which exports a function of exactly that name.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: The dialog heading renders its Title parameter; every caller passes a descriptive question (the bookings page passes 'Cancel this booking?'). The markup shows a Razor expression, not placeholder text. (Promoted from scanner noise in scan iteration 3, framework-on pass.)

entries.label: score-band
entries.rationale: No accessibility assertion in tests, no browser accessibility check, nothing in CI: the bottom rung of any enforcement ladder.

entries.label: score-band
entries.rationale: Model-judged. Of the images with a static, non-empty alt, all but one carry a meaningful description; the foyer illustration's alt is its file name (BA-023). Expected around 75; wide band for judge variance.

entries.label: score-band
entries.rationale: Model-judged. Link and button texts state their purpose ('Book a room', 'Cancel booking', 'Save settings', ...); one 'click here' link (BA-024) among a few dozen.

entries.label: score-band
entries.rationale: Model-judged. Headings and labels name their section or field ('Your bookings', 'Number of attendees', ...); one label reads 'Value' (BA-025) among a few dozen.

entries.label: clean
entries.rationale: No planted defect and no trap for the repository's themed concepts: every image, control, label, heading, interaction, ARIA attribute, colour pair, focus style, animation, dialog, medium and form error here is correct, no markup is rendered unsanitised, every string-named interop call resolves, and the judged texts are descriptive.
